_about: The mercy hub (plan 7.6f), built for review and not yet shown. Rows as in love.json and righteousness.json, built by tools/concepts/hub_build.py into out/concept-hubs/mercy.json. The rows stand on the ἔλεος family and the Hebrew רחם family; different words the English also renders mercy or compassion (חמל, חוס, חנן, σπλαγχνίζομαι, οἰκτιρμός and the rest) are named apart under 'others', each with its verses. Almost every row is filled by hand ('pick'), because the frames hold no usable agent for these verbs (Matt 9:27 gives the agent as 'son', the vocative) and miss six verses whose verb stands in an infinitive or participle (Hab 3:2, Rom 9:16, Rom 12:8, Jude 22, Jude 23, Lam 4:10's adjective): a rule would have filed the wrong verses and lost those. Divine persons are by hand throughout: a row about the LORD, God, the Lord or Christ lists verses where the text names him.

titles.noun: What the text says of mercy

_words_why: THE WORDS (decided 2026-10-10). The card held ἔλεος alone; its own family is ἔλεος, ἐλεέω, ἐλεήμων, ἐλεεινός and the negatives ἀνέλεος, ἀνελεήμων (Jas 2:13, Rom 1:31). The Hebrew words that the text itself pairs with them are the רחם family: רָחַם (verb), רַחֲמִים (noun), רַחוּם (adjective), the Aramaic רַחֲמִין (Dan 2:18) and רַחֲמָנִי (Lam 4:10, 'compassionate women'). The pairing is in the text: Hos 1:6 and 2:23 name 'No Compassion' (Lo-ruhamah), and 1 Pet 2:10 says 'once you had not received mercy, but now you have received mercy' (ἐλεέω). NOT here, and why: חֶסֶד is the word the Greek Old Testament is commonly said to render with ἔλεος (not checked here: the graph holds no Septuagint), and the Berean prints 'loving devotion' for it, almost always; it is the love hub's 'other word', and the Berean prints 'mercy' for it in a handful of verses (Hos 6:6, Mic 6:8, Ps 23:6, Neh 13:22). A different word the English also calls mercy goes apart (brief, rule 2), so it is listed under 'others' where the builder finds it, and Hos 6:6 / Mic 6:8, the card's own key verses, are shown as key verses and not placed in a row. חנן (be gracious: Ps 51:1 'Have mercy on me, O God' is this word), חמל and חוס (spare, pity), נחם (relent, comfort), σπλαγχνίζομαι (moved with compassion: Jesus' compassion in the Gospels), οἰκτιρμός, οἰκτίρω, οἰκτίρμων, ἱλάσκομαι, ἵλεως are different words and stay apart. ἐλεημοσύνη is 'alms', not mercy in the Berean's text. כַּפֹּרֶת and ἱλαστήριος are the 'mercy seat', an object, and are kept out by the pattern on the gloss ('mercy' not followed by 'seat'). SENSE: 'merc|compassion|pit'. It drops רחם as 'loved' (Ps 18:1) and as the name 'Ruhamah', and the one stray רַחֲמִים glossed 'emotion' (Gen 43:30).

others._why: Different words that the Berean's English also renders mercy, compassion or pity, named apart with their verses (brief, rule 2). min_n 1 so that a word the Berean glosses 'mercy' only once or twice still shows (חֶסֶד in 1 Kgs 20:31; the card's own list had Dan 4:27 and Dan 6:11, h2604). h337 and h1886 are gloss strays: אִי 'woe!' at Eccl 4:10 ('pity the one who falls') and the article ה, glossed 'Dothan' at Joel 2:17 and Neh 13:22 (the real words there are חוּס and חֶסֶד). The pattern leaves out 'mercy seat'. LIMIT, reported: the builder reads MACULA's gloss, not the Berean's printed text, so a word the Berean prints as 'mercy' but MACULA glosses otherwise (חֶסֶד in Hos 6:6, Mic 6:8, Ps 23:6; תַּחֲנוּן 'cry for mercy' in Ps 28:2, 86:6, 130:2) does not appear here.
others._others_patch: NOT READ BY hub_build.py (reported as a builder gap): 'add' is the hand list the builder cannot take, applied to out/concept-hubs/mercy.json after the build by scratchpad hubs/mercy_others_patch.py, and lost on a rebuild until the builder reads this key. Panel fix, 2026-10-10: the builder reads MACULA's gloss, so it shows חֶסֶד at 2 verses and misses the two where the Berean prints 'mercy' in the verses people come for (Hos 6:6, Mic 6:8, the card's own key verses); and it misses the Psalmists' 'cry/plea for mercy', תַּחֲנוּן, which MACULA glosses 'supplication'. Both are different words, shown apart, never in a row.

h2617.note: The Berean prints “mercy” for חֶסֶד in a few verses: here (Ps 23:6, 1 Kgs 20:31) and in Hos 6:6 and Mic 6:8, the verses people come for. Everywhere else it prints “loving devotion”. The rows of this page are built on another word; חֶסֶד is set out under Love.

h8469.note: תַּחֲנוּן, “supplication”: the Berean prints “cry for mercy”, “plea for mercy” in these verses. Another word, from the root of חנן (be gracious), set out here beside the rows.

h8467.note: תְּחִנָּה, “supplication”: the Berean prints “cry for mercy” at Ps 6:9 and “no mercy” at Josh 11:20.

others.title: Other words translated “mercy”, “compassion” and “pity”

_own_words_why: Panel fix, 2026-10-10 (Doug's ruling via the coordinator): key verses are verses of the hub's OWN words. Each checked in the original: Exod 34:6 רַחוּם, Ps 103:13 רָחַם, Lam 3:22 רַחֲמִים, Matt 5:7 ἐλεήμων/ἐλεέω, Matt 9:13 ἔλεος, Rom 9:15 ἐλεέω, Eph 2:4 ἔλεος, Jas 2:13 ἔλεος. Luke 6:36 is NOT an own word (οἰκτίρμων), so it is not here; it is pointed to from 'Show mercy to others'. Hos 6:6 and Mic 6:8, the card's own key verses, are חֶסֶד in the Hebrew and are out of the key verses; they are held by hand in the חֶסֶד entry under 'others' (see _others_patch), with a pointer to Love.

Hos.14.4.why: the frames file the fatherless finding compassion under MACULA's Hos 14:4; the Berean prints it at 14:3 ('For in You the fatherless find compassion'), and Hos 14:4 as shown is 'I will freely love them'

_review: Not yet reviewed. Flagged by the committee (2026-10-09, committee-flags.json) as low: the hub was Greek-only and a reader might take it for complete; keep the phrases as written; link out to the Hebrew steadfast-love rows and do not merge them; the works of mercy (alms) are a Catholic and Orthodox emphasis not in the grouping. This spec adds the Hebrew רחם family, names חֶסֶד apart, and leaves ἐλεημοσύνη out because the Berean prints 'alms'.
_regrouped: Regrouped from 35 rows to 23 at the coordinator's request (rule 8: about 15-25 rows). Nothing dropped: every verse of the 35-row spec is still in a row or in a 'Every other use' row (old spec saved as mercy_spec_35rows.json in the scratchpad hubs folder). Merged: the 'No Compassion'/'Not My People' pairing (its verses stay in the LORD, received-mercy and no-compassion rows; the pairing is in the received-mercy row's _why); 'A father, a mother, a son' (Isa 49:15 now in the verb catch-all, Matt 17:15 under 'Have mercy on me', Ps 103:13 and Jer 31:20 under the LORD row); the two verb 'bare He / the Lord' and 'eyes of others' rows into the verb catch-all, which now carries the bare-'He' note; 'Justice, judgment and mercy' with 'Anger, and mercy'; 'His great mercy' with 'The mercy of the LORD, of God'; 'The mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ' with 'The Lord grant mercy'; 'Remembering mercy', 'On those who fear Him' and 'Mercy in the eyes of others' into the noun catch-all; 'Mercy to one another' with 'No mercy shown'; 'The merciful, and the merciless' with 'Compassionate people'.

rows.label: “Have mercy on me, on us”
rows.note: The cry in the Gospels, to Jesus, and from the rich man to Abraham; “my son” in Matt 17:15. The Hebrew cry of Ps 51:1, “Have mercy on me, O God”, is another word, חָנַן, set out under Other words (see Grace).
rows._why: the cry in the Gospels, 11 verses by hand. Ten are made to Jesus ('Son of David', 'Lord', 'Master'); Luke 16:24 is the rich man to Abraham. Matt 17:15 is 'have mercy on my son'. Ps 51:1 'Have mercy on me, O God' is חנן, a different word (under others)

rows.label: The LORD will have compassion
rows.note: Hos 2:23, “I will have compassion on ‘No Compassion’”, is answered in 1 Pet 2:10 (“Now you have received mercy”, below); the same name stands under “No compassion” at Hos 1:6.
rows._why: by hand: verses where the LORD, God or the Lord is the one who has compassion, named in the verse or by the surrounding passage. Named in the verse: Deut 13:17, 30:3, 2 Kgs 13:23, Ps 103:13, 116:5, Isa 14:1, 30:18, 49:13, 54:8, 54:10, 55:7, Jer 30:18, 33:26, Lam 3:32, Ezek 39:25, Hos 1:7, Zech 10:6. Named only by the passage (the verse says 'I' or 'You'): Ps 102:13 and Hos 14:3 and Mic 7:19 (addressed to Him), Isa 60:10, Jer 12:15 and Hos 2:23 ('I', the LORD's speech in the passage). Isa 49:10 says only 'He who has compassion' and is left in 'Every other use', as the brief asks for a bare 'He'. Listed for the panel in the report.

rows.label: “I will have mercy on whom I have mercy”
rows.note: The text's own phrase, kept as written; Rom 9:23, “the vessels of His mercy”, continues the passage. Where Christian traditions part on how God's mercy bears on election and on human choice, the page takes no side.
rows._why: Rom 9:23 (a noun, ἔλεος) added 2026-10-10 by the panel: it is the other half of Rom 9:15-18 and was in the noun catch-all without the no-side note; it stays there too

rows.label: “Now you have received mercy”
rows.note: 1 Pet 2:10, “once you had not received mercy, but now you have received mercy”, answers Hosea's “No Compassion” (Hos 1:6 and 2:23). Each verse gives its own reason, or none; the page takes no side on what mercy depends on.
rows._why: the text's own passives: who received it and why is in the verse (Paul 'in ignorance and unbelief'). Prov 28:13 ('whoever confesses and renounces them will find mercy') moved to 'Compassion, and forgiveness' by the panel: it is a future conditional, not mercy received, and that row already holds the question and its note. 1 Pet 2:10 first, as the label's own words

rows.label: Show mercy to others
rows.note: Luke 6:36, “Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful”, is another word (οἰκτίρμων), set out under Other words.
rows._why: Matt 5:7 'they will be shown mercy' is the reciprocal; Rom 12:8, Jude 22 and 23 are not in the frames (infinitive and participle) and so are reached only by hand

rows.label: Mercy through disobedience
rows.note: The text's own words, kept as written: where Christian traditions part on whom Rom 11:32's 'everyone' takes in, the page takes no side.

rows.label: No compassion, no mercy, no pity
rows.note: Zech 1:12 is a question put to the LORD, “How long?”; the verses of this row are said of the LORD, of the enemy He raises, or asked of Him. Hos 1:6, “No Compassion”, is answered at Hos 2:23 and in 1 Pet 2:10.
rows._why: set beside the rows of mercy, as the text sets them (Hos 1:6 then 1:7). Said of the LORD (Isa 9:17, 27:11, Jer 13:14, Hos 1:6, 2:4), of the enemy He raises (Isa 13:18, Jer 6:23, 50:42, Jer 21:7 of Nebuchadnezzar), and asked of Him (Zech 1:12 'will You withhold mercy')

rows.label: Every other use
rows.note: Isa 49:10 says only “He who has compassion”, and Mark 5:19 says “the Lord”; readers take Mark 5:19 of the Father or of Christ, and the page does not choose.
rows._why: takes what no row above does: Isa 49:10, Isa 49:15 ('lack compassion for the son of her womb'), Mark 5:19, 1 Kgs 8:50 and Jer 42:12 (mercy 'in the eyes of' captors and a king). Its note carries the bare-'He' ruling of the 35-row spec

rows.label: Mercy and peace

not_verses.Jer.16.5: a withdrawal, not a greeting ('I have removed from this people My peace, My loving devotion, and My compassion'); it stands in 'Compassion beside חֶסֶד' and 'Mercy shown, and no mercy shown'

rows.note: The openings of 1 Tim, 2 Tim, 2 John and Jude, and Gal 6:16. On who “the Israel of God” is, readers part, and the page takes no side.

rows.label: Compassion beside חֶסֶד, “loving devotion”
rows.note: The Hebrew חֶסֶד, which the Berean renders “loving devotion” (“favor” in Dan 1:9), stands in these verses beside the Hebrew word for compassion. They are two words, and the page sets them side by side as the verses do.

rows.label: Beside justice, judgment and anger
rows._why: by hand, two old rows joined. 'Justice, judgment and mercy' (the rule on κρίσις and מִשְׁפָּט: Matt 23:23, Jas 2:13, Hos 2:19, Zech 7:9; Ps 119:156 was excluded because מִשְׁפָּט there is 'ordinances') and 'Anger, and mercy' ('In Your wrath, remember mercy', 'Has His anger shut off His compassion?', 'I was angry ... You showed them no mercy'). Hab 3:2 is not in the frames and is reachable only by pick

rows.label: The mercy of the LORD, of God
rows._why: by hand, two old rows joined ('His great mercy, His great compassion' and 'The mercy of the LORD, of God'). The text itself names the LORD or God as the one whose mercy it is in all but Neh 9:19, 9:27 (a prayer addressed to Him) and Isa 54:7 (the LORD's own 'I'). Left out because the verse names no one: Luke 1:50, Ps 79:8, Ps 103:4, Ps 119:77, Hos 2:19, Titus 3:5, Neh 9:28
rows.note: Phrases kept as written. Where readers part on who is meant by “the Lord” in a verse that does not say, the page does not choose.

rows.label: “Our Lord Jesus Christ”, “the Lord”
rows.note: Jude 21 names our Lord Jesus Christ. 2 Tim 1:16 and 1:18 say “the Lord”; readers take that of the Father or of Christ, and the page does not choose.

rows.label: Compassion, and forgiveness
rows.note: Set side by side as the text has them: where Christian traditions part on whether forgiveness waits on repentance, the page takes no side.

rows.label: Not our deeds, but His mercy
rows.note: The text's own words, kept as written: where Christian traditions part on mercy and works, and on what “the washing of new birth” is, the page takes no side.

rows.label: “I desire mercy, not sacrifice”
rows.note: Hosea 6:6, in the Hebrew: חֶסֶד, printed “mercy” there and usually “loving devotion” (see Love). Jesus quotes it in Matthew, where the Greek word is ἔλεος. This hub's rows are built on the Greek ἔλεος and the Hebrew רחם words; Hosea's word is set out under Love.

rows.label: Asking for mercy
rows._why: by hand: the verses that ask for it ('May God Almighty grant you mercy', 'Remember, O LORD, Your compassion', 'plead for mercy', 'receive mercy'). The cry 'Have mercy on me' of the Gospels is its own row under the verbs

rows.label: Mercy shown, and no mercy shown
rows._why: two old rows joined: 'Mercy to one another' (Zech 7:9 'Show loving devotion and compassion to one another', Luke 10:37 'The one who showed him mercy') and 'No mercy shown' (Isa 47:6, Amos 1:11 'stifled all compassion', Jer 16:5 'I have removed ... My compassion', Jas 2:13 'judgment without mercy'). Jas 3:17 ('full of mercy') is not mercy to another and stays in the catch-all

rows.label: Every other use
rows.note: Rom 9:23 belongs with Rom 9:15-18 (the verb row “I will have mercy on whom I have mercy”) and Rom 11:31 with Rom 11:30-32; where Christian traditions part on those passages, the page takes no side.
rows._why: takes what no row above does: Luke 1:50 ('His mercy extends to those who fear Him', with Ps 103:13 in the verbs), Luke 1:54 and 1:72 (remembering mercy / the covenant; Hab 3:2 is above), 2 Chr 30:9, Ps 106:46, Dan 1:9 and Jer 42:12 (mercy 'in the eyes of' captors, an official, a king), 1 Kgs 3:26, Rom 9:23, Rom 11:31, Jas 3:17, Isa 63:15, Neh 9:28, Prov 12:10

rows.label: The LORD is compassionate, merciful
rows.note: Jas 5:11, “The Lord is full of compassion and mercy”, is other words (πολύσπλαγχνος, οἰκτίρμων), set out under Other words.

rows.label: A merciful and faithful high priest
rows._why: the verse says 'He'; the sentence before it (Heb 2:9) names Jesus

rows.label: The merciful, the merciless, the compassionate
rows.note: Ps 112:4 is read of the upright man or of the LORD; the page does not choose.
